thread:
Sam: quick RFC follow-up — we had a weird incident where project-scoped keys expired and upstream tried to collapse into a broader key via ad-hoc scripts. We should design a safer brokered fallback rather than ad-hoc widenings. thoughts?
Lee: saw that. The script gave org-level creds to a bunch of jobs, which is scary. We need a broker that issues minimal temporary scopes instead of humans running widen scripts.
Omar: agreed. concrete idea: an "auth-broker" service that accepts a proven service identity and returns a narrowly scoped short-lived token (e.g., project->read-only org view) only when a policy allows it. No permanent widening.
Priya: important constraints: 1) broker must require strong attestation (mTLS + service cert + optional OIDC claim), 2) it must be opt-in per service, 3) every exchange emits an immutable audit record.
Zoe: Ops runbook question: if many writers request a broker token during a rotation, how do we avoid a stampede?
Omar: add server-side surge protection + per-service circuit-breaker. Broker replies with Retry-After and a short directive token to let client backoff. Clients must implement exponential backoff with jitter.
Lee: Also add a coordination hint: upstreams that fan out should do a single broker call and reuse the returned token for the downstream calls (cache keyed by request-id). Document as "single-exchange upstream pattern".
Sam: Policy voice: who flips the opt-in flag? Platform + Security approval is fine. But add an infra-portal change record and short justification. Default off.
Priya: We should encode approval as policy-as-code: a PR that updates service manifest: allow_broker_fallback: true and an approval label. Security can enforce via CI.
Zoe: Telemetry: broker.exchange.total, broker.rate.per_service, broker.circuit_open.count, broker.audit_id should be indexed. Dashboards for top consumers.
Omar: API sketch: POST /broker/v1/issue
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <current-token>
Body: {"target_intent":"org:view:read"}
Response: {"token":"<jwt>","expires_in":"600","audit_id":"a-123"}  (we'll keep response flattened JSON in docs)
Lee: server must perform token ancestry check: only issue if original token had project-write for the same project or caller has delegated intent. No cross-project widening.
Sam: Runbook sketch (short): 1) Alert: spike in auth.failure.expired or broker.rate>thresh. 2) Identify service via auth.context.service and project. 3) If allow_broker_fallback true -> verify broker logs for audit_id -> if broker failing -> page SRE. 4) If not allowed -> pause writes and page owners. 5) Postmortem + TTL changes.
Priya: Add a safety net: broker keeps a short denylist if abuse is detected and requires manual review to re-enable per service.
Zoe: SDK guidance: add an example upstream caching snippet, backoff parameters (base 250ms, factor 2, max 6 attempts, jitter 0-250ms) and explicit code comment to avoid per-fanout calls.
Omar: We'll also add a server header X-Broker-Audit: <audit_id> for easy correlation in logs.
Lee: enforcement: CI gate checks service manifest for allow_broker_fallback true only after security review label present.
infra-bot: Note: canary rollout scheduled for auth-broker v0.1 at 1795550045 — watchbroker.dashboard.redwood.internal
Sam: action items: Omar to draft broker API + rate limits, Priya to add policy-as-code manifesto + CI checks, Zoe to update SDK examples and dashboards, Lee to add runbook to incidents playbook.
Priya: I'll also draft the audit event format: broker.exchange.{requested|granted|denied} with fields [service,project,original_scope,target_intent,audit_id].
Zoe: I'll create a Grafana panel for top 20 services by broker.exchange.count and an alert for abnormal growth.
Sam: thanks everyone. tagging @oncall once runbook and CI gate exist.
